priors.applicability: Prefer when the observed square-hole fixture has translated or rotated relative to the demonstrations, while the peg remains securely closed-grasped, axis-near-aligned, and the requested hole-relative Cartesian path is reachable from the measured Panda joints. This is the primary displacement prior and covers high final alignment, descent, initial engagement, full +hole-x insertion, and terminal stabilization.

handoff.entry_conditions: Peg is visibly retained in a closed grasp and clear of the box; peg axis is near the hole axis; current hole, peg, TCP, and measured joints are finite. The demonstrated entry is high above the fixture, with peg z about 0.420-0.428 m, including an observed y-offset case near 0.160 m in demo12205.
handoff.exit_conditions: Keep the supplied task success definition unchanged: peg head x in [-0.145,-0.09], y/z within 0.009 m of the hole criterion, axis alignment at least 0.985, and a stable held pose. Demonstrated terminal peg centers are about (-0.182,0.1767-0.1769,0.0982-0.0983) m only for the demonstrated fixture pose; this prior transports the relation with the observed hole.
handoff.failure_signatures: IK nonconvergence or limit contact after a large fixture move; peg/TCP relative-pose separation; descent while laterally or angularly misaligned; fixture collision or stalled +hole-x progress. Nominal data do not support jam recovery.
handoff.overlap_role: Train every assigned action. The [1380,1500) interval overlaps reorient_and_stage_peg by 120 actions (6 s) in each of 12 demonstrations, retaining alignment, descent, and early engagement supervision for switch-time tolerance.
handoff.successor_readiness: There is no learned successor. Continue stabilization until the unchanged success geometry is observed; otherwise report failure rather than opening the gripper.

priors.limitations: Hole-relative equivariance cannot make a translated fixture reachable or collision-free. Absolute hole pose and measured qpos/qvel remain inputs for robot/workspace dependence, but the demonstrations contain one fixed hole pose and only successful insertions. The policy has no contact truth and no evidence for dropped pegs, large orientation errors, collision recovery, or jam retries.
priors.pipeline_implications: The high-level agent should route displaced but reachable fixtures here. Resolve hole_pose fresh in build_inputs and at every decoded execution step, retain measured joints for IK, keep the gripper closed, and stop only under the supplied success evaluator. If relative grasp integrity degrades, prefer the TCP-residual prior only when the peg is still visibly held; do not infer recovery support.
priors.rationale: The largest expected deployment shift is fixture displacement: all 12 training holes are at the same world pose, so world targets can memorizeize it. Encoding commanded TCP poses in the observed hole frame makes the complete align-descend-insert-hold trajectory equivariant to hole SE(3) displacement by construction. Observed qpos/qvel and absolute hole pose preserve reachability and robot-configuration dependence rather than asserting full task invariance.
priors.statement: Hole-frame SE(3) Cartesian trajectory prior: diffuse absolute TCP targets as hole-relative translation plus projected 6D rotation and gripper command, while conditioning on hole-relative TCP/peg/goal geometry, grasp geometry, absolute hole pose, and measured Panda state.

priors.applicability: Prefer when the fixture remains within the demonstrated/reachable neighborhood but the predecessor hands off at a perturbed TCP pose, measured tracking lags the nominal path, or the switch occurs at a different intermediate point while the peg is still securely held and there is no collision/jam signature.

handoff.entry_conditions: Peg is visibly retained, gripper remains closed, hole and TCP poses are finite, and the TCP perturbation is small enough that a local Cartesian correction remains reachable and collision-free. Entry may occur anywhere in the shared 1380-1500 alignment/descent/engagement interval.
handoff.exit_conditions: Use only the unchanged task success geometry and stable hold. Local residual magnitude is diagnostic, not a new success test.
handoff.failure_signatures: Repeated large residuals, accumulating drift from the hole goal, lateral error during descent, peg/TCP separation, IK nonconvergence, fixture collision, or stalled insertion. Re-anchoring is not demonstrated jam recovery.
handoff.overlap_role: All actions remain supervised, including 1,440 overlap actions across [1380,1500). Relative targets are encoded against each action observation, so early and late handoffs receive consistent local correction labels.
handoff.successor_readiness: No learned successor exists. Continue closed-gripper stabilization after geometric success; if residual re-anchoring drifts from the destination, hand control to the hole-frame prior rather than release.

priors.invocation_contract: {"call_args_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"destination_object":{"type":"string","enum":["hole"]},"held_object":{"type":"string","enum":["peg"]}},"required":["destination_object","held_object"],"additionalProperties":false},"parameter_semantics":"destination_object selects hole_pose for relative goal/error inputs; held_object selects peg_pose for grasp and phase geometry. Learned actions are local TCP corrections and neither argument is an actuator value."}
priors.limitations: The demonstrations contain nominal successful tracking, not injected disturbances. Re-anchoring each command to the fresh measured TCP is expected to reduce sensitivity to local execution error, but can drift or reproduce an unsafe local direction under large unseen offsets. It does not create contact sensing, grasp recovery, or jam recovery, and large fixture displacement is better covered by the hole-frame policy.
priors.pipeline_implications: Select this policy for secure-grasp local handoff/tracking variation. decode_action must compose each predicted TCP-frame delta with the fresh current TCP before shared IK; it must not integrate denoising calls or stale chunk state. Monitor destination-relative geometry externally and switch to the hole-frame prior if absolute goal anchoring is being lost.
priors.rationale: The demonstrations show measured TCP lag relative to commanded TCP throughout descent and insertion, and the predecessor may switch anywhere in a 120-action overlap. Encoding each demonstrated target as a delta from that slot's measured TCP and decoding against the fresh measured TCP creates a feedback-like local command representation, reducing dependence on the exact nominal intermediate state. It deliberately trades global anchoring for local correction robustness.
priors.statement: Fresh-TCP residual servo prior: diffuse local SE(3) corrections as current-TCP-frame translation, relative rotation vector, and gripper command; compose each executed slot with the freshly observed TCP and solve IK from freshly measured joints.

priors.applicability: Prefer when the hole is near the demonstrated world workspace but invocation phase is ambiguous: the predecessor may hand off high during descent, near the insertion line, after engagement, or already near stable completion. All object poses and robot state must remain within a plausible reachable, collision-free regime.

handoff.entry_conditions: Peg is closed-grasped and visible; hole, target, peg, TCP, qpos, and qvel are finite. The hole should be near its demonstrated world pose because this model predicts world-frame targets. Entry can be early, during insertion, or late in the stable tail.
handoff.exit_conditions: Only the supplied head-x interval, y/z tolerance, minimum axis alignment, and stable held pose define success. The inferred phase is guidance and never a success substitute.
handoff.failure_signatures: Stage logits conflict with visible geometry; world targets do not follow a moved fixture; descent begins with lateral/axis error; insertion stalls; peg separates from TCP; or IK reports nonconvergence/limits. No class denotes jam recovery.
handoff.overlap_role: The complete assigned segments are trained. The 1380-1500 overlap contains high alignment, descent, insertion-line settling, and initial +x motion, supplying multiple observable phases to both adjacent skills.
handoff.successor_readiness: There is no learned successor. A hold phase should preserve the closed grasp, but the framework evaluates readiness only from unchanged task geometry and stability.

priors.limitations: The auxiliary stages are deterministic labels from nominal geometric progress and do not establish contact. They may be wrong for collisions, jams, dropped pegs, or unusual approaches. World-frame absolute actions intentionally retain the demonstrated robot/workspace pattern and are not fixture-displacement invariant; the hole-frame prior covers that shift. Auxiliary supervision supports but does not replace diffusion.
priors.pipeline_implications: Use this model for uncertain switch timing near the nominal fixture pose. The trainable causal encoder and stage head must be registered, optimized, EMA-saved, and feed the diffusion condition; masked cross-entropy is auxiliary to active action diffusion. Route materially displaced holes to the hole-frame prior and local tracking perturbations to the fresh-TCP residual prior.
priors.rationale: A two-frame observation can occur in qualitatively different responsibilities: high descent, insertion-line advancement, or terminal hold. The trajectories show a z-dominant transition from about 0.42 m to 0.10 m, then +x insertion from peg center near -0.31 m to -0.182 m, followed by repeated stabilization targets. A causal phase auxiliary objective forces a learned encoder used by diffusion to preserve those distinctions, while absolute world Cartesian actions retain configuration/workspace regularities that the invariant policies may discard.
priors.statement: Causal phase-aware world-target prior: use a registered geometry encoder with an auxiliary approach/insert/stabilize head that conditions the diffusion backbone; diffuse absolute world TCP position, projected 6D rotation, and gripper command.
